title: Diagnosing Evidence Utilization in Multimodal Document Question Answering

problem.claim: It is unclear how effectively multimodal large language models use provided evidence during document question answering.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal document QA systems require clearer diagnosis of evidence utilization across different evidence types.

contributions.claim: A controlled empirical study evaluates 7 popular MLLMs on long multimodal multi-document question answering in a retrieval-augmented generation setting.
The study analyzes performance differences across text, image, table, chart, and cross-evidence inputs, including the effects of supervised finetuning.
An attention-based analysis examines how models allocate attention across image evidence, text evidence, system prompts, questions, and output tokens.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Zero-shot performance varies substantially across evidence types, with stronger reliance on text evidence and weaker performance on image-only and cross-evidence inputs.
Supervised finetuning produces limited and dataset-dependent improvements and often preserves existing evidence-type disparities.
Lower attention allocation to image tokens is associated with weaker performance on image-based evidence.

narrative_sequence.summary: The effectiveness of evidence use by MLLMs in document QA is unclear.
The authors conduct a controlled study of 7 MLLMs on long multimodal multi-document QA with RAG.
Performance differs substantially by evidence type, with reliance on text and weaker image-only and cross-evidence performance.
Finetuning yields limited, dataset-dependent gains and attention analysis links low image-token attention with weaker image-evidence performance.
The findings identify limitations in current multimodal document understanding.

source_observation.claim: Models perform more weakly on image-only and cross-evidence inputs than on text-based evidence.

interpretation.claim: Evidence modality and cross-modal integration are likely important determinants of multimodal QA reliability.

application.claim: Evaluate evidence-grounded systems separately by evidence type rather than relying only on aggregate QA performance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this pattern generalizes beyond the studied models, datasets, or task setting.

source_observation.claim: Supervised finetuning often preserves evidence-type disparities, while low attention to image tokens is associated with weaker image-based performance.

interpretation.claim: Improving multimodal evidence use may require addressing modality-specific attention allocation rather than applying finetuning alone.

application.claim: Use attention diagnostics alongside performance evaluation when investigating modality-specific failures.

exception.claim: The abstract reports an association, not a causal relationship between image-token attention and performance.
